# Platform settings (reference)

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_settings.py from config/settings.json. Do not edit by hand: change the registry and run  python tools/gen_settings.py  -->

Every number the platform uses as a limit, a default or a time lives in **one registry**: [`config/settings.json`](../config/settings.json). This page is generated from it (170 settings in 18 groups), so it is always current. The reasoning is in [SETTINGS_PLAN.md](SETTINGS_PLAN.md).

## How to read it

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Default** | The value the platform ships with. Nothing changes until someone changes it |
| **Range** | The lowest and highest value that makes sense. From plan step S2 the platform refuses anything outside it; today it is the documented safe range |
| **Scope** | `runtime`: read by the platform's own code (changeable without redeploying the AWS stack once S2 exists); `deploy`: part of the AWS stack (change it with the install tool, then `plan` and `apply`) |
| **Risk** | `low`, `careful` (can raise the AWS bill or affect capacity) or `security` (changes who can get in and for how long) |

## How to change a setting today

1. **`deploy` settings** that are template parameters (for example `gateway.inflightGlobal`): pass them to the install tool or edit the parameter default in `template.yaml`, then `plan` and `apply`.
2. **`runtime` settings:** change the `default` in `config/settings.json`, run `python tools/gen_settings.py`, run the tests, and publish the update (`node setup.mjs upgrade`).
3. A portal page and a command that change runtime settings without touching code are the next steps of the plan (S2 and S3).

A test (`tests/test_settings.py`) makes sure this registry, the code and the CloudFormation template agree, and that no new number is added to the code without being added here.

## Publishing a site (frontend)

How big a student's published site may be, and how long visitors' browsers and the CDN keep it.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `frontend.maxZipMB`<br>Largest upload (zip) | 50 MB | 1 to 500 | runtime | low | The biggest zip file a student may publish as their site. Bigger sites are refused with a clear message. |
| `frontend.maxUnzippedMB`<br>Largest site once unpacked | 200 MB | 1 to 2,000 | runtime | careful | The total size of all files in a published site after unzipping. Protects against zip bombs and storage growth. **Cost:** Raising it raises S3 storage and CloudFront transfer. |
| `frontend.maxFiles`<br>Most files in a site | 2,000 files | 10 to 20,000 | runtime | low | The number of files in one published site. |
| `frontend.cdnCacheSeconds`<br>How long the CDN keeps a file | 86,400 seconds | 60 to 2,592,000 | runtime | low | CloudFront keeps a file at most this long. A publish clears it at once, so this only matters if that clearing ever fails. |

## Student backends

The small server-side function each student may publish: its size, memory, time, logs and environment variables.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `backend.maxZipMB`<br>Largest backend upload (zip) | 50 MB | 1 to 50 | runtime | low | The biggest zip a student may publish as their backend. AWS allows at most 50 MB zipped (and 250 MB unzipped) for a function. |
| `backend.maxUnzippedMB`<br>Largest backend once unpacked | 250 MB | 1 to 250 | runtime | low | Total size of a backend's files after unzipping. AWS itself allows at most 250 MB. |
| `backend.maxFiles`<br>Most files in a backend | 500 files | 10 to 5,000 | runtime | low | The number of files in one backend upload. |
| `backend.memoryMB`<br>Memory of a student's backend | 3,008 MB | 128 to 3,008 | runtime | careful | The memory each student backend function is given when it is published (applies to backends published after the change). AWS accounts start with a cap of 3,008 MB per function (this account was checked); a quota increase raises it. **Cost:** Memory is billed per second of running time; double the memory is about double the cost per request. |
| `backend.timeoutSeconds`<br>Time a backend request may take | 27 seconds | 1 to 29 | runtime | careful | How long one backend request may run before it is stopped. AWS's HTTP front door ends every request at 30 seconds; the platform keeps 2 seconds of margin for the hop through its gateway, so 27 is the highest safe value. **Cost:** Longer requests cost more and hold platform capacity longer. |
| `backend.logRetentionDays`<br>How long backend logs are kept | 7 days | 1 to 365 | runtime | low | Days a student backend's log lines stay available (the logs command and the teacher view). **Cost:** Logs are billed per stored GB. |
| `backend.runs`<br>Backend runs allowance | 5,000 runs | 0 to 1,000,000 | runtime | low | Default runs allowance a student gets when the teacher enables the backend (maximum a teacher may set is the upper range). **Cost:** Each run costs a small amount of Lambda time. |
| `backend.maxEnvVars`<br>Most environment variables | 20 variables | 1 to 50 | runtime | low | How many environment variables a student may set on their backend. |
| `backend.maxEnvBytes`<br>Size of all environment variables | 4,096 bytes | 256 to 4,096 | runtime | low | Total size of a backend's environment variables. AWS allows at most 4096 bytes. |
| `backend.logLines`<br>Log lines returned | 50 lines | 1 to 100 | runtime | low | Default and largest number of log lines returned by one logs request. |
| `backend.logMinutes`<br>Log look-back window | 60 minutes | 1 to 180 | runtime | low | Default and largest number of minutes of log history one request looks at. |
| `backend.logPageEvents`<br>Log events read per page | 500 events | 50 to 1,000 | runtime | low | Events read from the log service in one call (up to pages x this many are read, then the newest are kept). |
| `backend.logPages`<br>Log pages read | 6 pages | 1 to 20 | runtime | low | How many pages of log events one logs request reads. |
| `backend.logCutChars`<br>Longest log message | 1,500 characters | 200 to 10,000 | runtime | low | A longer message keeps its end (the real error is at the end of a traceback). |
| `backend.logMinSecretChars`<br>Shortest environment value that is masked | 6 characters | 3 to 20 | runtime | careful | An environment variable value shorter than this is not hidden in logs (too many false hits). |
| `backend.reservedConcurrency`<br>Reserved concurrency per student backend | 0 executions | 0 to 100 | deploy | careful | 0 means none. On a new AWS account the limit is 10 so nothing can be reserved; the gateway's request limits protect the account instead. |

## Gateway and rate limits

The front door every student backend request passes through: size limits, requests at once, requests per visitor.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gateway.maxBodyKB`<br>Largest request body | 1,024 KB | 1 to 5,120 | runtime | low | The biggest request a visitor may send to a student's backend. |
| `gateway.maxResponseKB`<br>Largest response | 1,024 KB | 1 to 5,120 | runtime | low | The biggest answer a student backend may return. AWS functions can return at most about 6 MB. |
| `gateway.leakSeconds`<br>When a stuck request counter is freed | 60 seconds | 10 to 3,600 | runtime | low | A requests-in-flight counter untouched this long while above zero is treated as leaked and reset. |
| `gateway.perIpPerMinute`<br>Requests per visitor per minute | 120 requests | 10 to 10,000 | runtime | careful | How many requests one visitor address may send to student backends per minute. |
| `gateway.inflightGlobal`<br>Requests at once, whole platform | 3 requests | 1 to 500 | deploy | careful | Student backend requests that may run at the same time on the whole platform. The installer sets it from your AWS account's real Lambda concurrency limit (see Capacity). Derived from the AWS Lambda concurrency quota by the installer. |
| `gateway.inflightPerStudent`<br>Requests at once, per student | 2 requests | 1 to 50 | deploy | careful | Student backend requests that may run at once for one student. Derived from the AWS Lambda concurrency quota by the installer. |
| `gateway.waitMs`<br>How long a busy request waits | 0 milliseconds | 0 to 1,500 | deploy | careful | When every slot is busy, how long the gateway waits for one to free up before answering busy. 0 answers at once. Derived from the AWS Lambda concurrency quota by the installer. |
| `gateway.cacheSeconds`<br>How long a backend lookup is remembered | 10 seconds | 0 to 300 | runtime | low | The gateway remembers which backend belongs to a site for this long. |
| `gateway.negativeCacheSeconds`<br>How long a missing backend is remembered | 2 seconds | 0 to 60 | runtime | low | How long the gateway remembers that a site has no backend. |

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `sessions.studentHours`<br>Student session length | 12 hours | 1 to 72 | runtime | security | How long a student stays signed in to the student page. |
| `sessions.maxFailedLogins`<br>Wrong passwords before a lock | 5 attempts | 3 to 20 | runtime | security | After this many wrong teacher passwords in a row the login is locked. |
| `sessions.lockoutMinutes`<br>How long a lock lasts | 15 minutes | 1 to 240 | runtime | security | How long the login stays locked after too many wrong passwords. |

The lowest and highest cap a teacher can set for one student are this setting's range. **Cost:** This is real money per student per period. |

| `storage.maxFiles`<br>Most stored files | 100 files | 1 to 10,000 | runtime | low | The number of files one student may keep. |
| `storage.maxCollections`<br>Most collection names | 50 collections | 1 to 500 | runtime | low | How many different collection names a student may ever use (each is remembered so the teacher can clear them). |
| `storage.dataMB`<br>Database space per student | 5 MB | 1 to 100 | runtime | low | Default database space a student gets; the upper range is the most a teacher may give one student. **Cost:** Stored data is billed per GB-month. |
| `storage.filesMB`<br>File space per student | 50 MB | 1 to 500 | runtime | low | Default file space a student gets; the upper range is the most a teacher may give one student. **Cost:** Stored files are billed per GB-month. |

| `storage.downloadSeconds`<br>Download link life | 300 seconds | 30 to 3,600 | runtime | low | How long a file download link stays valid. |

| `knowledge.student.passages`<br>Passages per student | 5,000 passages | 100 to 60,000 | runtime | low | Default number of searchable passages a student's books may produce. **Cost:** Passages are stored and searched; more passages cost more to read and keep. |

| `knowledge.library.stored_mb`<br>Class library: space | 1,000 MB | 1 to 10,000 | runtime | low | Storage of the class library. **Cost:** Stored books are billed per GB-month. |

| `knowledge.uploadSeconds`<br>Book upload link life | 600 seconds | 60 to 3,600 | runtime | low | How long a book upload link stays valid. |
| `knowledge.staleUploadSeconds`<br>When an unused upload is forgotten | 3,600 seconds | 300 to 86,400 | runtime | low | An upload form nobody used is forgotten (and its book slot freed) after this long. |

| `knowledge.cacheDays`<br>How long search data is cached | 90 days | 0 to 365 | runtime | low | Days a computed search vector is reused instead of being bought again. **Cost:** A shorter time means more embedding cost. |
| `knowledge.apiMaxBodyChars`<br>Largest knowledge API request | 20,000 characters | 1,000 to 1,000,000 | runtime | low | The biggest request the knowledge API accepts from a student's backend. |
| `knowledge.maxAppSpans`<br>Steps an app may report per search | 30 steps | 0 to 200 | runtime | low | How many trace steps an app may report along with one search. |
| `knowledge.maxFileMB`<br>Largest book the reader accepts | 50 MB | 1 to 100 | runtime | low | The largest file the book reader will process. |
| `knowledge.maxPages`<br>Most pages in a book | 1,500 pages | 10 to 10,000 | runtime | low | A book with more pages is refused. |
| `knowledge.maxPassages`<br>Most passages in a book | 6,000 passages | 100 to 60,000 | runtime | low | A book that would produce more passages is refused. |
| `knowledge.minPageChars`<br>Smallest real PDF page | 40 characters | 1 to 1,000 | runtime | low | A PDF page with fewer characters than this is treated as a scan with no text. |
| `knowledge.pseudoPageChars`<br>Size of a pseudo-page | 3,000 characters | 500 to 20,000 | runtime | low | Text, Markdown and HTML have no pages, so they are cut into pieces of about this size for citing. |
| `knowledge.cacheShelves`<br>Shelves kept in memory | 6 shelves | 1 to 50 | runtime | low | How many shelves one warm search function keeps in memory. |
| `knowledge.cachePassages`<br>Passages kept in memory | 60,000 passages | 1,000 to 600,000 | runtime | low | Never more passages than this are kept in memory in total. |
| `knowledge.rebuildTries`<br>Tries to rebuild a search index | 3 tries | 1 to 10 | runtime | low | How often a failed rebuild is retried before giving up. |
| `knowledge.minSimilarity`<br>Meaning match needed to answer | 0.55 0 to 1 | 0.1 to 0.95 | runtime | careful | How close in meaning the best passage must be for the books to answer. Higher means the app says it does not know more often. A starting point; calibrate per shelf from an evaluation set on real books. |
| `knowledge.minCoverage`<br>Word match needed to answer | 0.6 0 to 1 | 0.1 to 1 | runtime | careful | Share of the question's words the best passage must contain for the books to answer. A starting point; calibrate per shelf from an evaluation set on real books. |
| `knowledge.embedBatch`<br>Texts per embedding request | 50 texts | 1 to 100 | runtime | low | How many passages are sent to the embedding service at once (Google accepts 100). |
| `knowledge.embedMaxTextChars`<br>Longest text to embed | 12,000 characters | 1,000 to 100,000 | runtime | low | About 3000 tokens; a passage is far smaller, so anything bigger is a mistake upstream. |
| `knowledge.workers`<br>Book readers at once | 2 readers | 1 to 10 | runtime | low | How many books may be read at the same time on the whole platform. **Cost:** Each reader holds a function execution for minutes. |
| `knowledge.monthlyCapUsd`<br>Monthly embedding budget | 3 US dollars | 0.0 to 1,000 | deploy | careful | The most the whole platform spends per month on turning books and questions into search data. **Cost:** This is real money per month. |
| `knowledge.embeddingModel`<br>Embedding model | gemini-embedding-001 | any | deploy | careful | The model that turns text into search data. Changing it means every book must be read again. |
| `knowledge.embeddingDims`<br>Embedding size | 768 dimensions | 64 to 3,072 | deploy | careful | The number of numbers per passage. Changing it means every book must be read again. The upper range is the model's limit. |

## Background jobs

Work that runs after the request has answered.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobs.perDay`<br>Background jobs per day | 20 jobs | 0 to 1,000 | runtime | low | Default jobs per day a student gets; the upper range is the most a teacher may give. **Cost:** Each job holds a function for minutes. |
| `jobs.concurrent`<br>Jobs at once per student | 1 jobs | 1 to 5 | runtime | low | Default number of jobs one student may run at once; the upper range is the most a teacher may give. |
| `jobs.minutes`<br>Minutes a job may run | 5 minutes | 1 to 15 | runtime | careful | Default minutes one job may run; the upper range is the most a teacher may give. AWS stops any function at 15 minutes. **Cost:** Longer jobs cost more. |
| `jobs.resultMaxKB`<br>Largest job result | 100 KB | 1 to 380 | runtime | low | The biggest result a job may save. |
| `jobs.payloadMaxKB`<br>Largest job input | 64 KB | 1 to 380 | runtime | low | The biggest input a job may be started with. |
| `jobs.listLimit`<br>Jobs per list | 20 jobs | 1 to 100 | runtime | low | How many jobs one list request returns. |
| `jobs.staleGraceSeconds`<br>When a silent job is failed | 300 seconds | 60 to 3,600 | runtime | low | A job that has not reported for this long past its time limit is marked failed. |
| `jobs.globalInflight`<br>Jobs at once, whole platform | 2 jobs | 1 to 100 | deploy | careful | Jobs that may run at once on the whole platform. Each holds a function execution for minutes, and a new AWS account allows only 10. |

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `traces.retentionDays`<br>Default trace retention | 90 days | 30, 60, 90 | runtime | careful | Default days a trace is kept before it is deleted automatically. The choices are 30, 60 or 90. |
| `traces.dailyLimit`<br>Traces per day per student | 2,000 traces | 0 to 100,000 | runtime | low | Default number of traces a student's app may record per day; the upper range is the most a teacher may give. **Cost:** Each trace is stored in the database. |
| `traces.maxTextChars`<br>Longest stored text | 4,000 characters | 100 to 20,000 | runtime | low | One stored text value is cut to this length. |
| `traces.maxItemBytes`<br>Largest stored step | 60,000 bytes | 1,000 to 300,000 | runtime | low | A stored step stays far below the database's 400 KB item limit. |
| `traces.maxAttrKeys`<br>Most details per step | 40 details | 1 to 200 | runtime | low | How many named details one step may carry. |
| `traces.maxSafeString`<br>Longest short detail | 80 characters | 10 to 500 | runtime | careful | A short detail kept even at the lowest privacy level is cut to this length. |
| `traces.maxSpansPerTrace`<br>Most steps in one trace | 200 steps | 5 to 1,000 | runtime | low | How many steps one trace may hold. |
| `traces.spansPerTraceBudget`<br>Steps allowed per trace | 20 steps | 1 to 200 | runtime | low | An app may report this many steps per allowed trace per day (daily limit times this), counted atomically. |
| `traces.clearBatch`<br>Traces removed per call | 100 traces | 10 to 1,000 | runtime | low | Traces removed per call of delete all of a student's traces (the teacher page repeats until done). |
| `traces.remindDays`<br>Days between retention reminders | 30 days | 1 to 365 | runtime | low | How often the teacher is reminded to download or clear old traces. |
| `traces.exportMaxTraces`<br>Traces per download page | 150 traces | 10 to 1,000 | runtime | low | How many traces one page of a download holds (AWS allows 6 MB per answer). |
| `traces.exportMaxBytes`<br>Size of a download page | 3,000,000 bytes | 100,000 to 5,000,000 | runtime | low | The size of one page of a trace download. |
| `traces.rollupKeepDays`<br>How long daily summaries are kept | 400 days | 30 to 3,650 | runtime | low | Days the per-day summaries (counts, cost, refusals) are kept. |
| `traces.driftMinAnswers`<br>Answers needed to judge a rate | 20 answers | 1 to 1,000 | runtime | low | A rate over fewer answers than this says nothing, so no alert is raised. |
| `traces.driftRefusalJump`<br>Rise in refusals that raises an alert | 0.15 0 to 1 | 0.01 to 1 | runtime | careful | Alert when the share of the books do not say answers is this much above last week's. |
| `traces.driftErrorRate`<br>Error share that raises an alert | 0.2 0 to 1 | 0.01 to 1 | runtime | careful | Alert when this share of answers had an error. |
| `traces.baselineDays`<br>Days of history for the baseline | 7 days | 1 to 60 | runtime | low | How many past days the usual rates are computed from. |

The optional small EC2 machine for platform-owned checks.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `worker.capMinutes`<br>Monthly machine minutes (class cap) | 2,400 minutes | 60 to 14,400 | runtime | careful | The most minutes the worker machine may run per month for the whole class. The range is the lowest and highest cap a teacher may set. **Cost:** The machine is billed per second while it runs. |
| `worker.maxMinutes`<br>Longest single run | 60 minutes | 15 to 360 | deploy | careful | The longest one run of the worker machine may last; a watchdog stops it after this. The range is the lowest and highest value allowed. **Cost:** Longer runs cost more. |
| `worker.instanceType`<br>Machine size | m7i-flex.large EC2 type | m7i-flex.large, c7i-flex.large, t3.small, t4g.small, c7g.large, c7g.xlarge, c7g.2xlarge | deploy | careful | The size of the worker machine. The default is one a Free plan AWS account may use; the c7g sizes need a paid plan. **Cost:** Bigger machines cost more per hour. |
| `worker.diskGb`<br>Machine disk | 30 GB | 20 to 200 | deploy | careful | Disk size of the worker machine. The disk is billed all month, even when the machine is off. **Cost:** About 8 cents per GB per month. |
| `worker.amiId`<br>Machine image | (empty) image id | any | deploy | low | The machine image the installer picked (x86 or ARM). Filled in by the installer. |

## Alerts and monitoring

When the platform tells the teacher something is wrong.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alerts.concurrencyThreshold`<br>Concurrency alarm level | 8 executions | 1 to .. | deploy | low | The alarm fires when this many function executions run at once (your AWS account limit is the ceiling). |
| `alerts.emailParameter`<br>Alert address (parameter name) | (empty) parameter name | any | deploy | low | The name of the AWS parameter that holds the e-mail address for alerts. The address itself stays in AWS. Empty means no alerts. |

## API request throttles

How many requests per second each platform API accepts.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `apiThrottles.backendRate`<br>Backend API: requests per second | 10 requests/second | 1 to 2,000 | deploy | careful | Steady requests per second the student backend API accepts. The installer sets it from the account's concurrency limit. Derived from the AWS Lambda concurrency quota by the installer. |
| `apiThrottles.backendBurst`<br>Backend API: burst | 20 requests | 1 to 4,000 | deploy | careful | Short burst of requests the student backend API accepts. Derived from the AWS Lambda concurrency quota by the installer. |
| `apiThrottles.deployRate`<br>Deploy API: requests per second | 20 requests/second | 1 to 2,000 | deploy | low | Steady requests per second the portal and deploy API accept. |
| `apiThrottles.deployBurst`<br>Deploy API: burst | 50 requests | 1 to 4,000 | deploy | low | Short burst the portal and deploy API accept. |
| `apiThrottles.storageRate`<br>Storage API: requests per second | 20 requests/second | 1 to 2,000 | deploy | low | Steady requests per second the class storage API accepts. |
| `apiThrottles.storageBurst`<br>Storage API: burst | 40 requests | 1 to 4,000 | deploy | low | Short burst the class storage API accepts. |

## Platform functions

Memory and time of the platform's own functions.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lambdas.deployMemoryMB`<br>Portal function memory | 1,024 MB | 128 to 10,240 | deploy | careful | Memory of the function that serves the portal and the deploy API. **Cost:** Billed per second of running time. |
| `lambdas.deployTimeoutSeconds`<br>Portal function time limit | 29 seconds | 3 to 29 | deploy | careful | Time limit of the portal function. The API front door stops at 29 seconds. |
| `lambdas.gatewayMemoryMB`<br>Gateway function memory | 256 MB | 128 to 3,008 | deploy | careful | Memory of the gateway function. **Cost:** Billed per second of running time. |
| `lambdas.gatewayTimeoutSeconds`<br>Gateway function time limit | 29 seconds | 3 to 29 | deploy | careful | Time limit of the gateway function. The API front door stops at 29 seconds. |
| `lambdas.storageMemoryMB`<br>Storage function memory | 256 MB | 128 to 3,008 | deploy | careful | Memory of the class storage function. |
| `lambdas.storageTimeoutSeconds`<br>Storage function time limit | 10 seconds | 3 to 29 | deploy | low | Time limit of the class storage function. |
| `lambdas.sweeperMemoryMB`<br>Nightly clean-up memory | 512 MB | 128 to 3,008 | deploy | low | Memory of the nightly clean-up function. |
| `lambdas.sweeperTimeoutSeconds`<br>Nightly clean-up time limit | 300 seconds | 30 to 900 | deploy | low | Time limit of the nightly clean-up function. |
| `lambdas.sweeperCron`<br>Nightly clean-up time | cron(0 3 * * ? *) cron | any | deploy | low | When the nightly clean-up runs (AWS cron format, in UTC). |

## Stored files and clean-up

How long the platform keeps leftovers.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `storageLifecycle.uploadsExpireDays`<br>Days an upload zip is kept | 1 days | 1 to 30 | deploy | low | Uploaded zip files are deleted after this many days. |
| `storageLifecycle.noncurrentVersionDays`<br>Days an old file version is kept | 30 days | 1 to 365 | deploy | low | Replaced or deleted file versions are kept this many days so a mistake can be undone. **Cost:** Old versions are billed as storage. |

## Feature switches

Which optional parts of the platform exist at all. Off by default; with a feature off nothing about it is created.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `features.backend`<br>Student backends | false true or false | false, true | deploy | careful | Turns on student backends, the gateway and the /api route. Off creates and changes nothing about backends. |
| `features.ai`<br>Class AI connector | false true or false | false, true | deploy | careful | Lets the teacher give a student's backend a capped, revocable AI key. Needs student backends. |
| `features.aiGemini`<br>Google Gemini for the class AI | false true or false | false, true | deploy | careful | Lets the teacher give a student Google Gemini instead of OpenRouter. Needs the class AI. |
| `features.storage`<br>Class storage connector | false true or false | false, true | deploy | careful | Gives students' backends a small database and file area with hard caps. Needs student backends. |
| `features.knowledge`<br>Class knowledge connector | false true or false | false, true | deploy | careful | Gives students' backends searchable books, and the class one shared library. Needs student backends. |
| `features.traces`<br>Traces | false true or false | false, true | deploy | careful | A step-by-step record of answers, stored per student and deleted automatically. Needs student backends. |
| `features.worker`<br>Compute worker | false true or false | false, true | deploy | careful | One small machine that is off by default, for platform-owned checks. With it off nothing is created. **Cost:** A few dollars a month when used. |

## Installation (set by the installer)

Names and ids the installer fills in. Normally changed only with the install and domain commands.

| Setting | Default | Range | Scope | Risk | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `install.rootDomain`<br>Platform domain | (empty) domain | any | deploy | low | The domain student sites are served from (for example apps.example.com). Empty serves them from the CDN address instead. |
| `install.certificateArn`<br>Certificate | (empty) certificate id | any | deploy | low | The certificate for the platform domain (must be in us-east-1). Required when a domain is set. |
| `install.portalAlias`<br>Portal address on the domain | false true or false | false, true | deploy | low | Attaches deploy.<domain> to the portal. Keep false on the first install until the DNS record exists. |
| `install.keysParameter`<br>Parameter holding the signing keys | /student-deploy/keys parameter name | any | deploy | low | The name of the AWS parameter that holds the students' access keys. |
| `install.teacherParameter`<br>Parameter holding the teacher password | /student-deploy/teacher parameter name | any | deploy | low | The name of the AWS parameter that holds the teacher's password hash. |
| `install.tenantDistributionId`<br>Custom-domain distribution | (empty) id | any | deploy | low | The CloudFront multi-tenant distribution used for students' own domains. Empty switches the custom-domain feature off. |
| `install.routingEndpoint`<br>Custom-domain routing endpoint | (empty) address | any | deploy | low | The routing endpoint of the custom-domain pieces. Filled in by the installer. |
| `install.connectionGroupId`<br>Custom-domain connection group | (empty) id | any | deploy | low | The CloudFront connection group the student domains join. Empty uses the default one. |

## Kept in code on purpose

These numbers are not settings: they are units, facts from a provider, or values that follow another setting.

| Where | Why it is not a setting |
|---|---|
| `ai.MICRO` | Unit conversion (one US dollar is a million micro-dollars), not a choice. |
| `portal.DAY` | Unit conversion (seconds in a day), not a choice. |
| `knowledge.MB` | Unit conversion (bytes in a megabyte), not a choice. |
| `storage.MB` | Unit conversion (bytes in a megabyte), not a choice. |
| `projects.MB` | Unit conversion (bytes in a megabyte), not a choice. |
| `traces.MS` | Unit conversion (milliseconds in a second), not a choice. |
| `storage_api.MAX_BODY_CHARS` | Derived: twice the largest stored value (storage.maxValueKB), so it follows that setting. |
| `embeddings.RETRY_DELAYS` | The back-off schedule (1, 2 and 4 seconds) for a failing embedding call: a design choice, not a limit. |
| `embeddings.DEFAULT_PRICES` | A price table for embedding models: facts from the providers, kept in code (or in the EMBEDDING_PRICES environment variable). |
| `gemini.DEFAULT_PRICES` | A price table for Gemini models: facts from the provider, kept in code (or in the AI_GEMINI_PRICES environment variable). |
| `worker.PRICES` | AWS hourly prices of the worker machine sizes: facts from AWS. |
| `worker.DISK_PER_GB_MONTH` | The AWS price of a disk per GB and month: a fact from AWS. |
| `worker.HOUR_CHOICES` | The 24 hours of a day (the daily start hour choices): not a choice. |
| `trace_core.RETENTION_CHOICES` | The retention choices the teacher page offers (30, 60 or 90 days): the values the format allows. The default is traces.retentionDays. |
